answer: Give every identity a willow test: each epoch it must publish a signed signal proving it completed one fresh task witnessed by two randomly drawn peers, while the tide of new identities is admitted only after passing the same test three epochs running. An honest agent does one task per epoch. An attacker with a thousand fakes must produce a thousand distinct witnessed signals every epoch, each costing a full task, so the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake and drowns in its own tide.
